subject.title: [Bug]:  [Windows] exec spawn: all commands hang with no output (stdio pipe deadlock)

question: Should maintainers prioritize a native Windows 11 and Node 24 reproduction run before allowing repair work on this exec hang?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the available evidence does not identify a current-main root cause or prove that recent Windows exec hardening fixes this reporter's timeout-hang symptom.

options.title: Run Native Windows Proof First
options.body: Use a real Windows 11 host with Node 24 to run a PowerShell-started gateway and capture `echo hello` plus `node -v` exec behavior before selecting a fix path.

options.title: Wait For Reporter Evidence
options.body: Keep the issue open but do not spend maintainer validation time until the reporter adds logs, screenshots, or a current-version repro transcript.

options.title: Defer As Stale Later
options.body: If no native proof appears after the issue is old enough for stale-insufficient-info cleanup, reconsider closing with a request for a fresh report.

recommendation.title: Run Native Windows Proof First
recommendation.body: Use a real Windows 11 host with Node 24 to run a PowerShell-started gateway and capture `echo hello` plus `node -v` exec behavior before selecting a fix path.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history across the central process helper and Windows exec invocation code.
